name: Mercedes-Benz
overview: The gold standard of luxury, safety, and performance in Australia, distinguished by historic local CKD assembly in Port Melbourne and world-leading AMG performance sales.
australian_history: Mercedes-Benz cars arrived in Australia in the early 20th century, but formal operations surged in 1958 when Mercedes-Benz (Australia) Pty Ltd was formed in partnership with Standard-Vacuum and Australian Motor Industries (AMI). From 1959 to 1965, Mercedes-Benz passenger cars—specifically the W120/W121 'Ponton' 190 and W110/W111 'Fintail' 220 and 220S—were assembled at AMI's factory in Port Melbourne, Victoria. Australia was one of the very few countries outside Germany to assemble Mercedes-Benz passenger cars. Local assembly concluded in 1965 as Daimler-Benz AG assumed full control of imports and distribution, establishing its headquarters in Mulgrave, Victoria. Mercedes-Benz pioneered automotive safety introductions in Australia, including crumple zones, anti-lock brakes (ABS in 1978), and electronic stability control (ESP). Australia also boasts one of the highest per-capita sales of Mercedes-AMG performance vehicles anywhere in the world, with models like the C63 AMG attaining legendary status.

models.name: E-Class
models.overview: The heartbeat of Mercedes-Benz in Australia. From the virtually indestructible W114/W115 and W123 that conquered outback roads and taxi fleets, through the peerless Bruno Sacco W124, to supercharged V8 E55 AMG and twin-turbo 450kW E63 S AMG monsters.

models.name: G-Class (Geländewagen)
models.overview: The immortal Mercedes-Benz Geländewagen. Originating as a relentless military off-roader with three locking differentials, the G-Class became a trusted explorer in the Australian outback and was selected by the Australian Defence Force under Project Overlander Land 121, resulting in over 2,000 bespoke Australian Army 4x4 and 6x6 vehicles. Concurrently, the civilian W463 morphed into the ultimate status symbol through the roaring twin-turbo V8 AMG G63.

g-class.segment: Heavy Duty 4WD / Upper Large Luxury SUV
g-class.overview: The immortal Mercedes-Benz Geländewagen. Originating as a relentless military off-roader with three locking differentials, the G-Class became a trusted explorer in the Australian outback and was selected by the Australian Defence Force under Project Overlander Land 121, resulting in over 2,000 bespoke Australian Army 4x4 and 6x6 vehicles. Concurrently, the civilian W463 morphed into the ultimate status symbol through the roaring twin-turbo V8 AMG G63.
g-class.australian_market_notes: First sold in Australia in 1982 (W460 280GE and 300GD). In 2008, the Australian Defence Force awarded Mercedes-Benz the Land 121 contract, purchasing over 2,000 W461 G-Wagens in 4x4 and Australian-exclusive 6x6 configurations. The G63 AMG accounts for the vast majority of civilian Australian sales.
